correctness.rationale: Off the absorbing set, the receptive pair selected for the proof can be chosen measurably, e.g. lexicographically. Strictly positive finite utilities make the two pre-noise displacements from x_i less than 2ε and 3ε, respectively. Of N centers spaced 5ε apart, each nonselected opinion blocks at most one within distance 2ε, leaving at least two. Each target window has length ε and lies within the claimed absolute noise bound (5N+4)ε after recentering, so the stated normal-density lower bound q applies separately to both noises. Such an update preserves old isolated vertices and creates two new ones. Counting every attempt and treating early absorption as a successful continuation, the conditional probability of absorption in m=floor(N/2) attempts is at least (q²/M)^m. This includes odd N because one remaining nonisolated vertex alone is impossible. The Markov property gives the claimed geometric tail and summing survival gives the mean bound. The threshold boundary is inactive, so X_t outside the absorbing set iff T>t; applying this under stationarity proves necessity of support, and sufficiency is immediate. Subtracting the two selected updates cancels the utility ratios, leaving (1−2μ) times the previous gap plus a fresh normal of variance 2σ². For a receptive start at μ=1/2, its two-sided exit probability is erfc(ε/(2σ)); the standard erfc equivalent gives the stated sharp reciprocal lifetime. An incompatible initial state instead has T=0. The finite checker is not required for any of these deductions.
residual_risks: The many-agent bound is a uniform upper bound, not a weak-noise equivalent. Background noise, clipping and changing confidence rules are outside the proof.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct claim is the all-state, finite-population freezing theorem for the unprojected microscopic conditional-noise chain, with a constructive state-uniform probability and exact invariant-law classification; the two-agent lifetime calibrates the theorem. The standard finite-block Markov argument and Gaussian complement calculation are not novel in isolation. The strongest inspected alternatives study a persistent-cluster diffusion, nonempty stabilized graphs under a different dynamics, or deterministic two-person overshoot. None yields a uniform route to an empty confidence graph under the frozen hypotheses.
residual_risks: Bounded priority assessment; an unindexed general theorem for conditional-noise absorption might subsume the argument.
The Steiglechner et al. and Shree et al. full texts were not available in the OA attempts; this is a remaining comparison limit, not negative coverage evidence.

value.rationale: The precise noise placement matters in a widely used type of confidence-gated model: an exact finite population can look like a persistent cluster for a long time yet its invariant probability laws give no mass to any receptive state. The constructive uniform bound resolves the infinite-time question despite unbounded opinion space and no global regularity of the utilities. The minimal sharp clock shows quantitatively why a weak-noise observation need not reveal this effect.
residual_risks: No sharp many-agent lifetime or empirical conclusion follows.
